text:
The S-curve tells you how far behind you are. It doesn't tell you where.

On a piping job, "74% actual vs 83% planned" starts the same meeting every week: which lines, which area, and what is holding them?

So I built a 4D playback for piping that answers it in one picture. Every spool carries two dates, its baseline erection week and its actual one, and the model colours itself week by week:

🟢 Erected on time
🟡 Erected late
🔴 Due, but still not erected
⚪ Not yet due

Press play and the plant builds itself against the baseline. Stop at the data date and you can see the delay sitting on the rack: Unit 215 is green, while the compression area is turning amber and red.

Hover a red spool and it tells you why: valves not received, isometric revision pending, spool still at the fab shop.

Same idea as my other dashboards: one HTML file, no Power BI licence, and no 3D software needed by the people who only want to look. It opens in a browser, even on a phone.

This demo runs on a fictional plant, the "Orion Project", with generated spools and dates. No client model and no client data.

Try it: https://osman2k4-dot.github.io/Dashboards/demo-piping-4d-playback.html

How do you show management where the piping delay is, and not only how big it is?
